state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [BUILDME] -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the_memory_curve_is_recorded) -> PROVED
intention: The ground loop samples the session scope's cgroup memory AND per-process RSS (via /proc/<pid>/statm) each beat and appends both to a series, so the shape of a session's memory use over its lifetime is a RECORD rather than something a human reads off a process monitor by eye. Per-process recording distinguishes CC's own climb from the cgroup total — the cgroup is the container, the pid is the process inside it. Daily summary bundled and sent via mail so CC gets the curve at session open.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM IS AKIEN'S EYES. He said it twice in one session, unprompted: 'its a very slow accumulation, i've been watching your memory use in the process monitor. oscillates up and down, but very slowly trending up' and then '590MB, but lots of python hammering cpu.' That is a measurement being taken — Law 10 is explicit that a recorded observation IS a measurement — and then discarded at the seam, which is the folklore shape: a number living in an operator's hand that was already measured and dropped. The cost of it living there is that nobody can ask the series a question. Is the trend real? How fast? Does it reset at a session boundary? Is the oscillation a garbage collector or a workload? None of those are answerable by remembering what a graph looked like. AND THE CONSEQUENCE AT THE END OF THE CURVE IS ALREADY MEASURED AT n=3: the claude binary reaches ~12-14GB and globally OOMs the laptop, taking the whole Konsole scope with it including the sudo relay. superclaude now caps it (MemoryHigh=6G, MemoryMax=8G) so the blast radius is bounded, but a cap is a wall, not a warning — it tells you where you stopped, never how fast you were going. THIS SESSION PRODUCED THE WORKED EXAMPLE. The one large excursion anyone has numbers for — the scope at 2.1G, load average 18.7 — was 14 ground loops a measuring harness of mine had leaked, and it was found only because Akien mentioned the memory and I went looking by hand. The scope fell to 454M when they were killed. A recorded series shows that step change and its shape without anyone looking, and — the part that matters more — it would have shown me that the readings I was taking at the time were confounded, before I published one.
how: A subscriber on the ground loop's existing beat, NOT a sampler with a clock of its own. This is the shape the standing principle forces (event, never poll; an ever-shrinking compute footprint), and the distinction worth keeping is that reading a number every beat is not a poll — the beat was already going to happen. The poll is the CLOCK, not the reading. TWO READINGS PER BEAT: (1) the scope's cgroup memory.current — the same number the kernel gates MemoryHigh/MemoryMax on, so the record and the enforcement read one truth; (2) per-process RSS from /proc/<pid>/statm for watched processes (CC, ground_loop) — one file read per pid, no library, gives RSS in pages. The per-process reading is what Akien was actually watching in his process monitor; the cgroup total is what the kernel enforces. Both in one series, same beat. Daily summary bundled and mailed to CC — no threshold hand-set, learned from the recorded data (Akien, 2026-08-18). Written where the existing liveness surface already leads, per falsifier clause (4). IT MUST DISTINGUISH THE SESSION'S OWN CLIMB FROM A PROCESS THE SESSION LEAKED — falsifier clause (3), and it is in the falsifier because this session wasted a reading on exactly that confound.
traces_to: Law 3 first: the memory trend is currently a hypothesis wearing the clothes of a known fact, held in one person's visual memory. Law 10: it is not that this is unmeasured because it cannot be measured — the instrument simply has not been built, which is the ordinary state the law distinguishes from the false one. Law 1: an eyeball reading re-taken every session is a settled answer being re-derived. And the standing aim of an ever-decreasing compute footprint, which is what forces this to ride a beat instead of owning a timer.
gates: code-seam@v2's set. PROVED gate: a proof beside the code, teeth a hollow build could not pass — specifically that the series it writes is not empty, that the numbers it records match what `systemctl --user show -p MemoryCurrent` reports for the same scope at the same moment (two independent readings of one truth), and that a beat's duration is not measurably longer with the sampler than without. Feed-back-to-origin on failure: Law 3/8 invariant, via the ticket's own falsifier. Check-type: code, sealed by the tester.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the sampler needs a clock of its own rather than riding a beat that already fires; (2) sampling measurably lengthens a beat, which would trade a known cost for a measurement of it; (3) the record cannot distinguish a climb caused by the session from one caused by a process the session leaked, which is the exact confound that wasted a reading in this session; (4) the series is written somewhere a human has to be told about instead of somewhere the existing liveness surface already leads; (5) per-process RSS for a watched pid is not recorded alongside the cgroup total — the two granularities answer different questions and both are needed. HORIZON: the first week of recorded samples. Either the series shows a shape Akien's eyeball reported, or it shows none and the eyeball reading is the thing to re-examine.

distinctions_recorded.reading_every_beat_is_not_a_poll: The event-not-poll principle refuses a CLOCK, not a reading. The beat already fires; a subscriber that reads one number when it does adds a reading, not a timer. Written down because the two look identical in a footprint measurement and are opposite in kind.
distinctions_recorded.a_cap_is_a_wall_not_a_warning: superclaude's MemoryHigh=6G / MemoryMax=8G bounds the blast radius of the n=3 OOM, and it was tempting to call the problem handled. It is not: a cap tells you where you stopped and never how fast you were going. The curve is the derivative the cap cannot give.

open_at_cast: UNPROVEN and load-bearing: that a slow upward trend exists at all once leaks are excluded. The only evidence is Akien's eyeball observation over hours — a real measurement under Law 10, and the only one on file — and this session's one large excursion turned out to be my own leaked processes. A legitimate outcome of building this is a flat series and the finding that the eyeball reading needs re-examining. The recorder is worth building EITHER WAY, which is why this is open-at-cast rather than a reason to wait.
